messages:
maria: ops-bot alert: high NVMe temperatures and iops degradation observed in eu-south2. ~48 nodes showing sustained temp ~80-85C, iops down ~30-45%. Linking perf dashboard https://dash.redwood.internal/r/evict/eu-south2 :rotating_light:
ops-bot: ALERT: nvme_temp_spike eu-south2 cluster=flashpack-2 count=48 peak_temp=85C iops_drop=40% severity=high
tom: seeing the gpu attach queue spike in eu-south dedicated pool. attach_latency 2x in last 10m. can we isolate nodes quickly?
jay: these are flashpack-2 nodes that got firmware 1.3.7 last night during the maintenance window — could be coincidental but worth flagging.
maria: fw 1.3.7 + nvme0 ecc counter uptick noted. sample from gnode-eus2-130: ```May  5 02:19:33 kernel: nvme0: retry=5 ecc_err=12 temp=84C status=0x23```
andrew: temp sensors show sustained 82-85C. thermal throttling will reduce throughput. ops reported AC spike at 02:14 UTC in the rack.
tom: thermal + fw skew makes sense. if nvme is throttling then batching and scrubbing will hurt gpu attach. ops, do we have a cooling ETA?
ops-bot: Ops ticket OP-5234 created: ac_unit_fault rack-eus2-row3. tech on site ETA ~45m
jay: proposal: cordon affected nodes and migrate GPU workloads off. We lose ~5% cluster capacity (48 nodes) but protects jobs. for Dedicated customers we can't live-migrate — need pod drain + reschedule.
maria: agreed. short plan: 1) cordon nodes (start with sample 10) 2) throttle background scrubs/evictions to lower IO 3) scale up temporary pool in eu-west1 to absorb critical traffic 4) collect nvme SMART and logs for vendor triage. tradeoff: cross-region absorb will increase cost.
andrew: note cost impact: if we autoscale 120 vGPUs in eu-west1 for 24h it's ~$7k/day. justify on SLA/customer impact.
tom: kicking off drain script on batch of 10 now: `scripts/drain-eu-south-thermal.sh --batch 10 --skip-preemptible`
jay: also run `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1 > /tmp/nvme-smart-gnode-eus2-130.log` and upload to the incident page. grabbing vendor contact.
maria: opening an incident page and tagging infra+oncall. incident INC-2026-347 created. I'll capture current perf hist and firmware mapping. we should consider fw rollback if correlation is strong. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-347 assigned to infra-oncall.
andrew: keep me in the loop. if this looks like firmware regression we need a rollback plan and customer comms template.
maria: noted — drafting rollback playbook and comms. will post in the incident doc once drafted.
